QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_4

question.text: Under SAS-100, the SIA issues an opinion titled 'Inherent Limitation' clause which, per the Chapter 8 sample report, states the report should NOT be construed as which of the following?

answer.text: An opinion, attestation, certification or other form of assurance
A case study for academic reference
Promotional material for the Social Enterprise
A baseline study for future projects

explanation.text: The Logic: The Chapter 8 sample Swagruha report's Inherent Limitation clause states verbatim: 'This report in no way should be construed as an opinion, attestation, certification or other forms of assurance. The procedures performed as part of the social impact assessment do not constitute an examination or a review in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards or attestation standards.' The SAS framework distinguishes impact assessment from audit/assurance. The Trap: Options B, C and D are not mentioned in the standard Inherent Limitation clause — only the assurance-disclaimer wording is boilerplate. Cross-Exam Context: Similar boilerplate appears in the Research Analyst disclaimer structure (XV) and the client-disclosure boilerplate in X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Paste the Inherent Limitation verbatim from the standard — do NOT paraphrase. Firms have been pulled up at peer review for diluting the 'not an opinion/attestation/certification' wording.
